levers.name: LR_DECAY
levers.effect: Scales each successive cosine restart cycle's peak by global run progress. At HEAD it is gated on `_n > 1` so it is a no-op for single-cycle schedules; on multi-cycle runs it multiplies `_cyc` (which already contains the `LR_MIN_FRAC` floor) by an envelope that itself bottoms at `LR_MIN_FRAC`, so the effective floor is `LR_MIN_FRAC²`.

levers.name: FAB_N0 / FAB_GROW / FAB_NMAX

levers.name: GROW_CAP family (GROW_CAP, _EVERY, _FAB, _FAB0, _VOCAB, _VOCAB0, _PLATEAU, GROW_LIFT, GROW_LIFT_MIN)
levers.effect: A soft cap below `FAB_NMAX`/`VMAX` that lifts on an earned plateau; nothing lowers it. `GROW_CAP=0` makes the whole family inert. `GROW_LIFT` is now a FRACTION of the current cap (0.08) with `GROW_LIFT_MIN`=8 as an absolute floor — its third incompatible unit system.

levers.name: TOK_COMPOSE / TOK_ANCHOR / TOK_ANCHOR_TAU / TOK_ANCHOR_USES
levers.effect: `TOK_ANCHOR` and its two release knobs are methods of `ByteComposer`, which is constructed only under `TOK_COMPOSE=1`. With `TOK_COMPOSE=0` they print on the EFFECTIVE line of every run and contribute nothing; the never-fired audit fires on every default run saying so.

levers.name: SEED_CKPT / GRID_CKPT / SAVE_CKPT
levers.effect: Whether a run leaves a checkpoint at all — and `SAVE_CKPT` also gates extra `holdout_bpb` passes, so toggling it once moved a same-seed result by 1.594 b/B. `SEED_CKPT` defaulted 0 while `GRID_CKPT` defaulted 1, so the sweep producing the models worth continuing from was the one discarding them.

levers.name: HOLDOUT_N / EVAL_N / PROBE
levers.effect: Report-only cadences that must not touch training. Before `c76dc74` they did: changing `HOLDOUT_N` 4→16 moved 48 report lines including a verdict sign flip, because `build_stream()` drew segment lengths from the global RNG that the diagnostics also drew from.

levers.name: RETOK_EVERY
levers.effect: Re-segmentation cadence. `RETOK_EVERY=0` did NOT stop re-segmentation (`_resample()` re-tokenises at every epoch boundary) and additionally disabled signature batching, because `_due` returns False on n<=0 before recording — so every `RETOK_EVERY=0` arm differed from its comparator in two ways.

levers.name: SIG_WIN / SIG_PROJ_BPT / SIG_SPACE
levers.effect: How much of the stream the signature encoder actually reads. `SIG_WIN=0` meant WIN bytes against a loop striding WIN tokens (~42% coverage, worsening as compression improves); `SIG_PROJ_BPT` pinned at 2.4 made projected coverage read 100% at every VMAX and suppressed the warning; `SIG_SPACE=tokens` crashed the first time a smoke arm exercised it.

levers.name: MANAGE_EVERY / DOM_MANAGE_EVERY / MANAGE_MERGE
levers.effect: `MANAGE_EVERY=500` was once longer than the whole run, so domain merge/cull/fold executed zero times on 60 kB and once on 120 kB; `DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=100` split domains onto their own cadence. `MANAGE_MERGE=0.12` overrode the `MERGE_FRAC*NEW_DIST`=0.28 fallback for the project's life, so creation ran at 0.35 and consolidation at 0.12.

levers.name: EVAL_GIST
levers.effect: Gates whether the eval path builds a real signature for the fabric to route on (`_eval_sig`) or falls back to the zero-gist placeholder. Default 1 at HEAD — this is what removes 06 §2's "routed without a real signature" limitation.

levers.name: WORLD_MODEL / WORLD_GROW / WORLD_FEEDBACK and the WORLD_* sizing family
levers.effect: The forward-dynamics world model, ON by default and costed every step, whose only full-stack readings all say it has not learned dynamics. The entire sizing family (`WORLD_HID/_K/_LAT/_N0/_NMAX/_ROUTE/_VAR`) has never been set, so it has only ever run in one shape.

carry_forward.why: It is why 'how much you measured decided what you trained on', why two arms differing in a training knob got different text in epoch 2, and it is the root cause of the levers-not-isolated problem the researcher raised seven times. The countermeasure (`frozen_rng()` / `@no_rng_drift` plus a dedicated stream generator seeded from `(SEED, epoch)`) must survive any rewrite of the eval battery.

carry_forward.item: Seed variance is a property of the ARM, not of the instrument. Across four arms of one 2x2 measured the same day on the same instrument, estimated σ ranges 0.047 to 1.225 — 26x — and instability tracks ramping. Never pool it.
carry_forward.why: It changes seed-budget arithmetic by orders of magnitude (D-vs-B ≈ 12 paired seeds; 2.009-vs-1.999 ≈ 1,450) and it means 'the noise floor' is not a single number anyone can quote. The corpus flags that whether the VARIANCE difference or the MEAN difference is the real phenomenon has never been asked, and the variance is the larger effect.

carry_forward.item: `_due` is not a predicate: it RECORDS the step and returns True, so calling it twice in one `if`/`elif` consumes the event. This killed re-segmentation entirely for three 18-epoch runs, was separately armed for `grow`, and its early-return on n<=0 silently disabled signature batching for every `RETOK_EVERY=0` arm.
carry_forward.why: Three distinct bugs from one helper's contract, and the third one is what makes the `frozen` vs `frozen_nr` pair — quoted in the source as the largest single effect on record — not a single-knob comparison. Any cadence helper in a rebuild needs this contract stated at its definition.

The corpus names `retire_stale`, `fuzzy_segment`, `track_usage`, `FAB_RESCUE`, `remap_mem_ctx`, the memory probe and the domain-prior section as instances, and now ships a count with every new maintenance path.
carry_forward.why: 05_ERRORS calls this "the single most transferable rule the record produces". It is the generalisation of the whole DID-IT-FIRE discipline and it is applied by construction in the current code.

carry_forward.item: A value can be wrong (banner), unread (typo), or read-but-unreachable — and each needed its own check because each is invisible to the others. The three layers are the derived `[config] EFFECTIVE` banner, the NOTHING-READ-THESE/not-verified audit, and the never-fired loss-term audit.

carry_forward.item: Purity rises MONOTONICALLY with fragmentation (one window per cluster scores 1.0); completeness falls with it; neither can see whether anything recurs. V-measure against the four seeded corpora is the WRONG target — the corpora are a scaffold, and V actively penalises the intended behaviour.
carry_forward.why: Weeks were spent steering by these metrics and the two headline results of that campaign were both retracted. The corpus' replacement headline is RECURRENCE (visits per domain, fraction visited once, fraction recurring ≥3 times), and domain counts/purity/silhouette/V/specialization are labelled DIAGNOSTICS, NOT TARGETS.

carry_forward.item: Prefer a RETRAINED ablation to an eval-time KNOCKOUT. They disagree badly: the FABRIC knockout said +0.709 b/B, the retrained pair said 3.089 vs 3.090.
carry_forward.why: The knockout number justified a default for two months and was retracted. This is the cleanest methodological lesson in the corpus and it is one line to state.

carry_forward.item: Every verdict needs a null (shuffled / permuted / matched-size), and the null needs an error bar. Two 4 MB runs differing only in SEED printed OPPOSITE informativeness conclusions against a hard cutoff of 0.010; the true null spread was ±0.020.
carry_forward.why: Every experiment in the record that shipped with a pre-specified null still stands; almost every one that did not, does not. This is the strongest predictor of survival in the whole corpus.

carry_forward.item: Quote every held-out figure against its OWN run's order-1 anchor, never against another row's. The corpus was re-fetched and order-1 moved 3.440 → 3.747; raw numbers suggested 18 epochs cost 0.34 b/B, own-anchor numbers say they bought and cost nothing (1.411 vs 1.441).
carry_forward.why: `runs.csv` has no corpus column, so raw `held_out` cannot be read down the table. `Δ order-1` is the only cross-corpus-comparable quantity and it is reproducible from the CSV to three decimals.

carry_forward.item: There is no single bits/byte scale marker across text and code: GPT-2-small is 1.0878 on Pile-CC, 1.1111 on OpenWebText2, 1.2253 on the Pile aggregate and 1.7912 on GitHub. Every Python result in this project was read against the web-text anchor and looked worse than it was.

carry_forward.item: `ACROSS THE RUN BOUNDARY` was a WEIGHTS-ONLY number: `holdout_bpb` → `_eval_logits` never consults the store. The literature's own framing: 'there is no weights-only version of BWT — you are computing BWT on a different, ablated system'.
carry_forward.why: It is the one number the continual-learning claim rests on, and the corpus' own §9 Step 0 prescribes the fix (report the matched pair R_full/R_weights so their difference IS the memory's contribution, and it separates an eviction problem from a forgetting problem). That fix is now in the code and the notes do not know it.

carry_forward.item: Plain reservoir sampling GUARANTEES the observed failure mode as a theorem: E[slots held by A] = M·N_A/N → 0 as a new domain streams indefinitely — 'the old domain is not evicted by a bad decision, it is diluted to zero by a correct one'. The remedy in the replay-CL literature is per-source / class-balanced quotas (CBRS, iCaRL); this project's partition is keyed on EXPERT, not domain, and both domains route to overlapping experts, so it is not a per-source quota.
carry_forward.why: It explains why every English memory entry vanished in the one continual-learning run, and it means the researcher's recorded rejection of a per-domain quota (`5c711cf`) should be re-decided rather than inherited. It also flags that this project is in the replay-CL regime, not the kNN-LM regime.

carry_forward.item: `EVICT=lru` (least-recently-RETRIEVED) was made the default before the test that would price it was run, and the caching literature says LRU-on-retrieval is precisely the pattern that field spent five years moving away from — a new domain flooding the store is the textbook SCAN pathology, which plain LRU has no defence against.
carry_forward.why: It is a live, cheap, internal test (compare the new domain's occupancy share under `EVICT=lru` vs `EVICT=recency` after a domain switch, using `mem_evict_test.py`'s existing harness shape) and it bears directly on the project's stated target.

carry_forward.item: Reading beat running by a wide margin: ~40% of catalogued defects were found by reading the code, and the five most expensive (`FABRIC=0`, `PHASED=0`, `MANAGE_MERGE=0.12`, `MEM_PER_EXPERT=1`, no culling at all) produced no crash and no implausible number. Running the same thing twice found what one run could not, every time it was tried, and it was tried rarely.
carry_forward.why: It is the operational conclusion of the whole error catalogue and it directly sizes where audit effort should go in any rebuild.

carry_forward.item: The automated drift check has a failure mode of its own: it rewrites history to satisfy a check about the present. At `0065372` it produced an altered verbatim commit quotation (06:94) and a historical table cell that contradicts its own column header (06:461), and its regexes still miss table cells and 'has X at Y' prose (07_WIP's LR_DECAY=0.0 survives).

carry_forward.item: A gate only covers what it exercises. The 12 kB smoke certified a change that killed both pilot arms in under two minutes; the `no_experts` gate arm was vacuous and had passed in every run since it was added; `_flags_for` defined inside a `case` branch would have resolved every smoke arm to the empty string, reporting seven identical runs as seven passing arms.
